instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Gal 6:13 desire (desire) stands four words before boast: the circumcision of others is what they want, and the boast in their flesh is its purpose.
observations.grounds: they desire to have you circumcised

observations.text: In Jude 16 desires (desire) stands three words before boasters, in the preceding clause: following their own sinful desires is listed with the inflated speech.
observations.grounds: following their own sinful desires

observations.text: In Obd 12 ruin (destruction) stands two words before boast, in the clause before it: the day of Judah's ruin is the day in which Edom is forbidden to gloat, rejoice and boast.
observations.grounds: in the day of their ruin

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:8 destroying (destruction) stands fourteen words after boast, negated, set against building you up: the authority Paul boasts of is not for destroying.
observations.grounds: not for destroying you

observations.text: In 1Cor 9:15 die (die) stands four words before boasting, in a comparison with rather than: Paul prefers death to losing his ground for boasting.
observations.grounds: I would rather die than have anyone deprive me

observations.text: In 1Cor 4:7 sees anything different (doubt) opens the verse, eleven words before boast: the first of three questions, who distinguishes you, leads to the question why you boast.
observations.grounds: who sees anything different in you

observations.text: In 2Cor 1:12 sincerity (earnest) stands fourteen words after boast, in the content of the boast: Paul's conduct with simplicity and godly sincerity is what his conscience testifies and he boasts of.
observations.grounds: simplicity and godly sincerity

observations.text: In 2Cor 9:2 zeal (earnest) stands eleven words after boast, in the closing sentence: the Corinthians' zeal, of which Paul boasts, has stirred up most of the Macedonians.
observations.grounds: your zeal has stirred up most of them

observations.text: In 1Cor 13:4 patient (endure) stands six words before boast, the first thing love is; boast is among what love does not do.
observations.grounds: Love is patient

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:12 continue (endure) stands ten words before boasted: Paul's going on with his conduct is set to undermine the opponents' claim made in their boasted mission.
observations.grounds: I will continue to do

observations.text: In Psa 10:3, Psa 75:4 and Psa 94:4 the wicked or the evildoers (evildoer) stand at or next to the boast as its subject or its parallel: the wicked boasts (Psa 10:3), the boastful are set beside the wicked (Psa 75:4), the evildoers boast (Psa 94:4).
observations.grounds: all the evildoers boast

observations.text: In Psa 52:1 and Jam 4:16 evil (evildoer) stands with the boast as its ground or its judgement: the mighty man boasts of evil (Psa 52:1), and all such boasting is evil (Jam 4:16).
observations.grounds: Why do you boast of evil

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:21 weak (faint) stands four words before the first boast, in Paul's ironic admission: too weak for what others did, he yet dares what they dare.
observations.grounds: we were too weak for that

observations.text: In Jer 49:4 faithless (faithless) stands two words after boast, naming the one addressed: the faithless daughter boasts of her valleys and trusts in her treasures.
observations.grounds: O faithless daughter

observations.text: In Heb 3:6 hold fast (fast) stands three words before boasting and governs it: the boasting with confidence is what is to be held fast, the condition of being his house.
observations.grounds: if indeed we hold fast

observations.text: In Isa 20:5 dismayed (fear) opens the verse, seven words before boast: dismay and shame come on those whose hope and boast were Cush and Egypt.
observations.grounds: they shall be dismayed and ashamed

observations.text: In Psa 49:13 foolish (folly) stands three words before boasts, naming the confidence of those whose path it is: the sayings approved after them are the boasts of the foolish.
observations.grounds: those who have foolish confidence

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:16, 2Cor 11:21 and 2Cor 12:6 fool or foolish (folly) stand a few words from Paul's boast and frame it: accepted as a fool so that he may boast a little (11:16), speaking as a fool between two dares (11:21), and he would not be a fool if he boasted, since he would speak truth (12:6).
observations.grounds: accept me as a fool

observations.text: In 2Cor 1:12 simplicity (folly) stands eleven words after boast, in its content: a word the folly collection holds stands here for singleness of conduct, a pairing of the collection with no folly in the verse.
observations.grounds: with simplicity and godly sincerity

observations.text: In Psa 34:2 glad (gladden) closes the verse, four words after boast: the humble are glad at the boast made in the Lord.
observations.grounds: let the humble hear and be glad

observations.text: In Psa 38:16 and Obd 12 rejoice (gladden) stands before the boast in the same chain: rejoicing over the one who falls and boasting against him are set together, asked against (Psa 38:16) and forbidden (Obd 12).
observations.grounds: let them not rejoice over me

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:9 gladly (gladden) stands two words after boast and qualifies it: the boast in weaknesses is made all the more gladly.
observations.grounds: boast all the more gladly

observations.text: In Psa 10:3 greedy (greed) stands three words after boasts, the subject of the parallel clause: the greedy one who curses stands beside the wicked who boasts.
observations.grounds: the one greedy for gain curses

observations.text: In Jam 3:14 selfish ambition (greed) stands five words before boast in the condition: where it is in the heart, the boast is forbidden.
observations.grounds: bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:30, 2Cor 12:5 and 2Cor 12:9 weakness (guard) stands a few words after boast as its object: what shows Paul's weakness, his weaknesses only, and, in 12:9, weakness first in the Lord's word where power is made perfect and then as the ground of the boast.
observations.grounds: except of my weaknesses

observations.text: In Psa 34:2 hear (hear) stands three words after boast: the humble hear the boast made in the Lord.
observations.grounds: let the humble hear

observations.text: In Zep 2:8 heard (hear) opens the verse, eight words before boasts, with the Lord as subject: he has heard the taunts and the boasts made against his people's land.
observations.grounds: I have heard the taunts of Moab

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:6 hears (hear) closes the verse, far after boast: Paul refrains from boasting so that no one thinks of him more than what is seen or heard from him.
observations.grounds: sees in me or hears from me

observations.text: In 2Cor 1:12 conscience (heart) stands five words after boast, named as the content of it: the boast is the testimony of conscience.
observations.grounds: the testimony of our conscience

observations.text: In 2Cor 5:12 heart (heart) closes the verse, six words after the second boast: the heart is named as what the opponents leave out of their boast, set against outward appearance.
observations.grounds: not about what is in the heart

observations.text: In Jam 3:14 hearts (heart) stands two words before boast: jealousy and ambition in the heart is the condition under which the boast is forbidden.
observations.grounds: in your hearts, do not boast

observations.text: In Psa 97:7 and Isa 20:5 shame (honor) stands just before the boast and falls on those who boast: the worshippers of idols (Psa 97:7), and those whose boast was Egypt (Isa 20:5).
observations.grounds: All worshipers of images are put to shame

observations.text: In Rom 2:23 dishonor (honor) stands three words after boast with God as object: the one who boasts in the law dishonours God by breaking it.
observations.grounds: dishonor God by breaking the law

observations.text: In 2Cor 7:14 and 2Cor 10:8 shame (honor) stands after Paul's boast and is negated: he was not put to shame by his boasts about the Corinthians (7:14), and will not be ashamed of boasting of his authority (10:8).
observations.grounds: I was not put to shame

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:21 shame (honor) opens the verse, before both dares: Paul's ironic shame at having been too weak precedes his daring to boast.
observations.grounds: To my shame, I must say

observations.text: In Isa 20:5 hope (hope) stands four words before boast in a parallel pair: Cush their hope and Egypt their boast.
observations.grounds: Cush their hope

observations.text: In 1Th 2:19 and Heb 3:6 hope (hope) stands next to boasting: listed with joy and the crown of boasting (1Th 2:19), and as the ground of the boasting held fast (Heb 3:6).
observations.grounds: our boasting in our hope

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:15 hope (hope) stands six words after the refused boast, opening the next clause: instead of boasting in others' labours Paul hopes for growth of their faith.
observations.grounds: But our hope is that

observations.text: In Jer 9:24 justice (impartial) stands nine words after the boast, among what the Lord practises: the boast is to rest on knowing the one who does justice.
observations.grounds: steadfast love, justice, and righteousness

observations.text: In Jude 16 showing favoritism (impartial) stands right after boasters: partiality for gain is set next to the inflated speech.
observations.grounds: showing favoritism to gain advantage

verses.text: They pour out their arrogant words; all the evildoers boast.
But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast and be false to the truth.
For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul, and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces the Lord.
But do not gloat over the day of your brother in the day of his misfortune; do not rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their ruin; do not boast in the day of distress.

But he said to me, “ My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
but Christ is faithful over God’s house as a son. And we are his house, if indeed we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in our hope.
Then they shall be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush their hope and of Egypt their boast.
As it is, you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
You who boast in the law dishonor God by breaking the law.
For who sees anything different in you? What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?
We are not commending ourselves to you again but giving you cause to boast about us, so that you may be able to answer those who boast about outward appearance and not about what is in the heart.
For whatever boasts I made to him about you, I was not put to shame. But just as everything we said to you was true, so also our boasting before Titus has proved true.
for I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the people of Macedonia, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year. And your zeal has stirred up most of them.
For even if I boast a little too much of our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for destroying you, I will not be ashamed.
We do not boast beyond limit in the labors of others. But our hope is that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you may be greatly enlarged,
And what I am doing I will continue to do, in order to undermine the claim of those who would like to claim that in their boasted mission they work on the same terms as we do.
I repeat, let no one think me foolish. But even if you do, accept me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
On behalf of this man I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except of my weaknesses —
though if I should wish to boast, I would not be a fool, for I would be speaking the truth; but I refrain from it, so that no one may think more of me than he sees in me or hears from me.
For even those who are circumcised do not themselves keep the law, but they desire to have you circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.
But I have made no use of any of these rights, nor am I writing these things to secure any such provision. For I would rather die than have anyone deprive me of my ground for boasting.
For our boast is this, the testimony of our conscience, that we behaved in the world with simplicity and godly sincerity, not by earthly wisdom but by the grace of God, and supremely so toward you.
For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at his coming? Is it not you?
To my shame, I must say, we were too weak for that! But whatever anyone else dares to boast of —I am speaking as a fool — I also dare to boast of that.
Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant
These are grumblers, malcontents, following their own sinful desires; they are loud-mouthed boasters, showing favoritism to gain advantage.
For I said, “Only let them not rejoice over me, who boast against me when my foot slips!”
“I have heard the taunts of Moab and the revilings of the Ammonites, how they have taunted my people and made boasts against their territory.
I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn;
My soul makes its boast in the Lord; let the humble hear and be glad.

To the choirmaster. A Maskil of David, when Doeg, the Edomite, came and told Saul, “ David has come to the house of Ahimelech.” Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The steadfast love of God endures all the day.
All worshipers of images are put to shame, who make their boast in worthless idols; worship him, all you gods!

but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the earth. For in these things I delight, declares the Lord.”
Why do you boast of your valleys, O faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, ‘ Who will come against me?’
This is the path of those who have foolish confidence; yet after them people approve of their boasts. Selah

2Cor 9:2: zeal at 16, boast at 5; your zeal has stirred up most of them.
